i0: We use ***be going to*** + base verb for **plans** we have already decided and for **predictions** based on what we can see now: *I**'m going to** learn Spanish. Look out! You**'re going to** fall!*
i1: To compare it with *will*, see [Will vs Going To](/blog/grammar/will-vs-going-to/). For arrangements with other people, see [Present Continuous](/blog/grammar/present-continuous/#pc-future).
bgt-form.t: I'm going to…: plans and intentions
bgt-form.s: **am / is / are going to + base verb** for things you've already decided to do: *I'm going to buy a new phone.*
bgt-form.b0.h: Subject | be | going to | base verb
bgt-form.b1: Use *be going to* for **intentions**: something you decided **before** speaking. *I**'m going to** clean my room this weekend.*
bgt-form.b2: Common time words: *tonight, tomorrow, this weekend, next week, next year, soon.*
bgt-form.b3: In fast, informal speech, *going to* often sounds like *gonna*: *I'm gonna call her.* Don't write *gonna* in formal English.
bgt-negative-questions.t: Not going to and Are you going to…?
bgt-negative-questions.s: Negative: **'m not / isn't / aren't going to**. Question: **Are you going to…? What are you going to do?**
bgt-negative-questions.b0.0.2: *I**'m not going to** go out tonight.*
bgt-negative-questions.b0.2.1: question word + be + subject + going to + verb?
bgt-negative-questions.b0.3.1: Yes, … am / is / are. No, … 'm not / isn't / aren't.
bgt-negative-questions.b1: Put *be* before the subject in questions: ***Is** she **going to** come?* Not *She is going to come?* (in writing).
bgt-evidence.t: Predictions from evidence: It's going to rain
bgt-evidence.s: Use **be going to** for a prediction based on something we can see or know **now**: *Look at those clouds. It's going to rain.*
bgt-evidence.b0: When there's **evidence now** that something will happen, use *be going to*: *Look at that car! It**'s going to** crash!* *She's pregnant. She**'s going to** have a baby in June.*
bgt-evidence.b1: The event is often very close, or we can see that it's starting: *I feel terrible. I think I**'m going to** be sick.*
bgt-evidence.b2: For predictions based only on opinion, *will* is common: *I think she**'ll** win.* For predictions from evidence, *going to* is more natural: *She's so far ahead. She**'s going to** win.* See [Will vs Going To](/blog/grammar/will-vs-going-to/#wvg-prediction).
bgt-vs-present-continuous.t: Going to or present continuous for plans?
bgt-vs-present-continuous.s: **be going to** = an intention (I've decided). **present continuous** = an arrangement (it's fixed with other people, a time and a place).
bgt-vs-present-continuous.b0.0.0: *I**'m going to** see a doctor.* (I've decided to.)
bgt-vs-present-continuous.b0.0.1: *I**'m seeing** the doctor at 4.* (I have an appointment.)
bgt-vs-present-continuous.b1: Often both are possible: *I**'m going to** visit / I**'m visiting** my aunt on Saturday.* The present continuous suggests the plan is **fixed** (my aunt knows, we've agreed a time).
bgt-vs-present-continuous.b2: Use *going to* (not the present continuous) when it's just an **intention**, with no arrangement yet: *One day I**'m going to** climb Everest.*
bgt-vs-present-continuous.b3: With *go* and *come*, people usually prefer the present continuous to avoid *going to go*: *I**'m going** to Spain next month* (more natural than *I'm going to go to Spain*).
bgt-vs-present-continuous.w0: an intention without arrangements: going to
bgt-was-going-to.t: Was going to: plans that changed
bgt-was-going-to.s: **was / were going to + base verb** = a past plan, often one that **didn't happen**: *I was going to call you, but I forgot.*
bgt-was-going-to.b0: Use ***was / were going to*** to talk about what you **intended** to do in the past: *We **were going to** take the train, but there was a strike.*
bgt-was-going-to.b1: Very often, the plan **didn't happen**, and we explain why with *but*: *I **was going to** go to the gym, **but** I was too tired.*
bgt-was-going-to.b2: It can also describe a past prediction: *I knew it **was going to** rain.*
bgt-was-going-to.b3: For more ways to talk about the future seen from the past, see [Future in the Past](/blog/grammar/future-in-the-past/).
x.bgt-vs-present-continuous-s03: A fixed arrangement: present continuous (*going to* is also possible).
q.bgt-was-going-to-s02: What does *We were going to buy that house* mean?
x.bgt-was-going-to-s02: *Were going to* = a plan that didn't happen.
x.bgt-was-going-to-s03: A plan that didn't happen: *was going to go*.
